title: Mutram Veedu
subtitle: A Chettinad-style courtyard home with thinnai, oonjal and a clay-tile roof

cover.alt: South Indian courtyard house at dusk with a clay-tile roof, teak pillars on the thinnai verandah and coconut trees

excerpt: A single-storey home built around an open mutram: thinnai at the front, oonjal in the hall, brass lamps at the pooja shelf, and a roof that pours the monsoon into the courtyard.
concept: Everything turns towards the mutram. The four roofs slope inward so light, breeze and rain all arrive at the tulsi madam in the centre — and the family gathers around it.
narrative: The brief came from a family that wanted the house of their grandparents' stories, but with a modern kitchen and fewer mosquitoes. We kept the bones of a Chettinad home: a raised plinth, a thinnai verandah facing the street, a carved teak door, and rooms arranged around an open courtyard.

The mutram is sunk a quarter of a metre below the floors and paved in stone. Six octagonal teak pillars on black granite bases carry the inner edge of the roof. The roof itself slopes two ways — outward to the eaves and inward to the courtyard — so the monsoon falls straight onto the tulsi madam.

The hall on the left has an Athangudi tile floor, an oonjal on brass chains and cane chairs for the evening coffee. The right wing has a red oxide floor, a teak dining table and a kitchen with a black granite counter and a shelf of brass and copper vessels. At the back, a pooja niche with two kuthuvilakkus is visible from the front door.
Every element was modelled and textured by a script in Blender for this portfolio. Mutram Veedu is a concept study and has not been built.

title: Oonjal Flat
subtitle: A Chennai apartment that swings

cover.alt: Apartment living room with Athangudi tiles, a teak oonjal by the windows and cane chairs

excerpt: A plain 2BHK living room gets Athangudi tiles, an oonjal by the window and a brass uruli — without breaking a single wall.
concept: Bring the village home into a city flat with three moves: a tile floor with a pattern, a swing where the breeze is, and brass that catches the evening light.
narrative: The flat had everything a builder flat usually has: beige vitrified tiles, a tube light in the middle of the ceiling and nowhere to sit that wasn't a sofa facing the TV. We replaced the floor with handmade Athangudi tiles and gave the window wall to an oonjal hung from the slab.

Cane chairs and a low teak teapoy face the sofa, so evening coffee becomes a conversation rather than a screen session. A Thanjavur-style panel hangs above the sofa; a kuthuvilakku stands in the corner for festival days.
Teak window frames replace the aluminium sliders and an ochre dado protects the walls from chair backs and children's cycles.
The before and after views are a visualisation study from identical Blender cameras, not photographs of a completed project.

title: Hotel Mallipoo
subtitle: A temple-town lobby that smells of jasmine

cover.alt: Hotel lobby with teak pillars, Athangudi floor, red silk sofas, a brass uruli and brass bell lamps

excerpt: Teak pillars, an Athangudi floor, red silk sofas and a giant brass uruli full of marigolds — welcome to Madurai.
concept: Arrival should feel like stepping into a cool mandapam on a hot afternoon: high ceilings, pillars, brass light and flowers floating in water.
narrative: The 5.6-metre lobby is organised like a temple mandapam. Four octagonal teak pillars on granite bases frame a central lounge; a cluster of brass bell lamps hangs at different heights above a 1.7-metre uruli filled with marigolds and jasmine.
Reception is a stone counter with a teak top, guarded by a tall kuthuvilakku that is lit every evening. A large Thanjavur-style panel in a gilded frame faces the entrance.
Sofas are upholstered in deep red silk with gold borders; cane chairs face them across the uruli so guests can wait, meet or simply watch the flowers.
This is a concept visualisation made for the portfolio; the hotel is fictional.

title: Kaapi Labs Studio
subtitle: A long table, a long window, and endless filter coffee

cover.alt: Office with a polished concrete floor, a long table and a ribbon window

excerpt: A ribbon window, a six-metre review table and a timber wall for a twelve-person design team.
concept: Replace the cubicle grid with one shared table. Quiet desks sit along the window; the table is where work is reviewed, argued over and finished — usually with coffee.
narrative: A 12-metre ribbon window runs the length of the north wall, giving even daylight to three individual desks. The centre of the room is a six-metre table under two linear pendants — the place where drawings are pinned, samples compared and lunch shared.

The west wall is lined in vertical timber boards that hide storage and soften acoustics. Opposite, a full-height shelf holds the library and sample archive, and a separate material table keeps current palettes on view.
Floors are polished concrete; the ceiling is left as exposed concrete. The palette is deliberately quiet so the work on the table is the most colourful thing in the room.
This is a concept visualisation. The office images on the Studio page come from the same Blender scene.

title: Mylapore Terrace House
subtitle: Saving a Madras-terrace roof, one teak joist at a time

cover.alt: Renovated room with a Madras-terrace ceiling of teak joists, exposed brick, red oxide floor and an oonjal

excerpt: Teak joists and brick kept as found; red oxide floor restored, a granite-topped kitchen added, and an oonjal by the window.
concept: Keep what the old house does well — the Madras-terrace roof, tall windows and honest brick — and add a kitchen and a swing that make it easy to live in again.
narrative: The house had been used as a storeroom for years: raw concrete patches over the floor, painted-over walls, tube lights and clouded window glass. Our study keeps the Madras-terrace roof — teak joists carrying brick and lime — and cleans the windows rather than replacing them.
A red oxide floor is relaid across the room. The brick wall is cleaned and sealed; the other walls are finished in lime plaster.

The kitchen is a single teak run with a black granite counter and green tiles, facing a granite-topped island with three cane stools. An oonjal hangs by the window, and a banana plant grows where the old water tank used to leak.
The before and after images use identical Blender cameras and are a design visualisation, not documentation of a completed project.
